lessons.title: Proofreading for clear meaning
lessons.description: Reread writing to find spelling, punctuation and sentence errors.
lessons.content: Proofreading is a final check for errors that can make writing difficult to understand. Check one kind of error at a time: sentence beginnings and full stops, spelling of familiar words, and whether each sentence is complete.
learning_objectives: Identify common punctuation and spelling errors.
Use a simple proofreading routine to improve a short paragraph.
prerequisites: Recognise capital letters and full stops.

explanation_sections.title: Check sentence boundaries
explanation_sections.body: Begin a sentence with a capital letter and use an appropriate ending mark. A full stop usually ends a statement. A question mark ends a direct question. Read the paragraph slowly to notice where one idea ends.

explanation_sections.title: Check words and meaning
explanation_sections.body: Look for common spelling patterns and reread each sentence to make sure it says what you intend. Ask someone to read it if a sentence is unclear. Recap: check punctuation, spelling and meaning in separate passes.

worked_examples.prompt: Correct: 'on monday we visited the library'
worked_examples.solution: On Monday, we visited the library.
worked_examples.reasoning: The sentence begins with a capital, the day name is capitalised, and the statement ends with a full stop.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Which correction makes 'where is my book.' correct?
questions.explanation: A direct question begins with a capital and ends with a question mark.

options: Finding errors and improving clarity in a final draft.
Changing every sentence into a question.
questions.correct_answer: Finding errors and improving clarity in a final draft.
questions.explanation: Proofreading checks writing for errors that interfere with clear reading.

questions.prompt: Which check helps a writer find a missing full stop?
options: Read each sentence and notice where its idea ends.
Count the colours on the page.
questions.correct_answer: Read each sentence and notice where its idea ends.
questions.explanation: Reading sentence by sentence helps identify missing sentence-ending punctuation.

lessons.title: Writing clear instructions
lessons.description: Arrange steps in order and use precise action words for a familiar task.
lessons.content: Instructions explain how to complete a task. They should name the task, put steps in a sensible order and use clear action words. Time-order words such as 'first', 'next' and 'finally' guide the reader.
learning_objectives: Sequence a set of steps in a logical order.
Use action verbs and time-order words in instructions.

explanation_sections.title: Order the steps
explanation_sections.body: Think about what must happen before the next action. For washing hands, wet hands before applying soap, and rinse after rubbing. Steps in the wrong order may make a task harder or less effective.

explanation_sections.title: Make actions clear
explanation_sections.body: Begin each step with an action verb such as 'place', 'mix' or 'rinse'. Add time-order words when they help. Recap: keep steps ordered, use precise verbs and include only actions needed for the task.

worked_examples.prompt: Put these actions into a sensible order: dry hands; wet hands; rinse soap; rub with soap.
worked_examples.solution: Wet hands; rub with soap; rinse soap; dry hands.
worked_examples.reasoning: The order follows the task from beginning to completion.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Which word best signals the last step in a set of instructions?
questions.explanation: 'Finally' tells the reader that the last step is coming.

options: Pour the clean water into the cup.
questions.correct_answer: Pour the clean water into the cup.
questions.explanation: It names a specific action and the object it acts on.

questions.prompt: Why should steps appear in a sensible order?
options: So the reader can complete the task correctly.
So the task has no beginning.
So the reader must guess every action.
So the title replaces the steps.
questions.correct_answer: So the reader can complete the task correctly.
questions.explanation: A logical sequence makes the instructions practical to follow.
